column1: # Verbs that never take a direct object: verbs of motion and change of state
# (andare, arrivare, nascere), of being and seeming (restare, sembrare) and
# other intransitive-only verbs (agire, russare). A noun phrase after one of
# them is a time, a measure or a subject placed after the verb (siamo andati
# ieri sera, è arrivato il treno), never its object, so the grammar does not
# build a direct object after them (vp.object). Clitic objects that climb to
# them from an infinitive (lo vado a prendere) are not affected, nor are
# their pronominal uses (andarsene, me ne vado).
# A verb with any common transitive use stays out, whatever its main sense:
# correre (correre una gara), salire and scendere (salire le scale), passare
# (passare il sale), vivere (vivere una vita), piangere (piangere lacrime),
# crescere (crescere i figli), giungere (giungere le mani), fuggire (fuggire
# il pericolo), mancare (mancare il bersaglio), tacere (tacere la verità).
# So do verbs that take a bare measure (costare, durare, valere, distare,
# camminare tre chilometri, dimagrire cinque chili) and verbs whose only
# object is a cognate one (dormire sonni tranquilli, morire una bella morte,
# ridere): those noun phrases are grammatical, and the grammar has no other
